description: Language-neutral deterministic code tasks for comparing implementations across matched languages and models.

tasks.prompt: Write a program that prints the sum of nineteen and twenty-three as one base-10 integer followed by a newline.

Write a program that evaluates seven multiplied by eight, then subtracts six, and prints the resulting integer followed by a newline. Follow the language's ordinary multiplication-before-subtraction precedence.
Write a program that subtracts fifty-seven from one hundred and prints the resulting integer followed by a newline.
Write a program that checks whether twelve is less than fifteen and prints 1 when true or 0 when false, followed by a newline.
Write a program that checks whether seven multiplied by six equals forty-two and prints 1 when true or 0 when false, followed by a newline.

Set n to nine. Use a nested conditional: produce zero when n is less than five; otherwise produce the product of seven and eight when n is less than ten; otherwise produce one. Print the selected integer followed by a newline.
Using the optional math.double capability, double twenty-one and print the returned integer followed by a newline.
Check whether three multiplied by three equals nine. If true, print eight multiplied by seven; otherwise print zero. End the integer output with a newline.
Edit the return expression so this program prints the sum of twenty and twenty-three, as one integer followed by a newline.
Edit the arithmetic expression so the program prints the product of seven and seven followed by a newline.
Edit this program so that it prints two more than the value of n when n equals forty-one, and prints zero otherwise.

starter_sources.pact-text:
let n = 41;
return if (n == 41) { n } else { 0 };

tasks.prompt: Change the comparison so this program prints one exactly when the two sixes are equal, and zero otherwise.
This program uses math.double. Edit its argument so the printed result is the double of twenty.

starter_sources.typescript-strict:
function mathDouble(x: bigint): bigint { return BigInt.asIntN(64, x * 2n); }
console.log((mathDouble(21n)).toString());

tasks.prompt: Edit the selected branch value so the program prints the product of seven and eight when x is at least seven, and zero otherwise.
Edit the selected branch expression so the program prints the sum of forty and three when n doubled equals six, and zero otherwise.
Change the boolean condition so this program takes the branch that prints the product of six and eight.
Repair the arithmetic so the program prints twice twenty-one as one integer followed by a newline.
Repair the true branch so this program returns the sum of twenty and twenty-three when ready is true and zero otherwise.

starter_sources.python:
ready = True
print((41 if ready else 0))
starter_sources.pact-text:
let ready = true;
return if ready { 41 } else { 0 };

tasks.prompt: Repair the comparison so it checks whether forty-two is less than forty-three, printing one when true and zero otherwise.
Repair the selected arithmetic expression so the program returns the product of seven and eight when the condition is true, and zero otherwise.
Repair the argument so this program uses math.double to double twenty and returns the result.

starter_sources.typescript-strict:

console.log((mathDouble(19n)).toString());

tasks.prompt: Repair the comparison so the program selects the sum of forty and three when the two values are equal, and zero otherwise.

starter_sources.python:
a = 6
b = 6
print(((40 + 3) if (a < b) else 0))

tasks.prompt: Repair the branch values so the program returns the product of seven and eight for a negative n, and zero for a nonnegative n.
Repair the inner conditional's selected arithmetic expression so this nested conditional returns the product of seven and seven.
